chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Foreword Bagnall and Frier have performed two extraordinary labors in their con- struction of this book.
text_raw:
Foreword 
Bagnall and Frier have performed two extraordinary labors in their con-
struction of this book.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: First, they have assembled about 300 original returns from censuses in Roman Egypt during the first to the third cen- turies.
text_raw:
First, they have assembled about 300 original 
returns from censuses in Roman Egypt during the first to the third cen-
turies.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: It has been possible to collect these returns in usable form because they were inscribed on papyrus.
text_raw:
It has been possible to collect these returns in usable form because 
they were inscribed on papyrus.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: After assembling these records (literally assembling them in some instances of crumbled documents), they have put them in order, and translated the inscriptions.
text_raw:
After assembling these records (literally 
assembling them in some instances of crumbled documents), they have put 
them in order, and translated the inscriptions.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Second, they have applied to this body of data the set of modern methods of inferring basic demographic characteristics from incomplete and inexact information.
text_raw:
Second, they have applied to 
this body of data the set of modern methods of inferring basic demographic 
characteristics from incomplete and inexact information.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: These techniques have been devised in recent years to enrich our knowledge of the character- istics of historical populations and the populations of contemporary less developed countries.
text_raw:
These techniques 
have been devised in recent years to enrich our knowledge of the character-
istics of historical populations and the populations of contemporary less 
developed countries.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: This combination of the skills of outstanding classical historians with the most refined techniques of modern demography is indeed unusual; the result is a clear picture of the age composition, mar- - rlage customs, fertility, and mortality in Egypt at the height of the Roman Empire.
text_raw:
This combination of the skills of outstanding classical 
historians with the most refined techniques of modern demography is 
indeed unusual; the result is a clear picture of the age composition, mar-
- rlage customs, fertility, and mortality in Egypt at the height of the Roman 
Empire.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: It is not a completely clear picture because of the limited size of the sample, and because of various kinds of bias in what is written on the returns, but still an exciting increase in our knowledge.
text_raw:
It is not a completely clear picture because of the limited size of 
the sample, and because of various kinds of bias in what is written on the 
returns, but still an exciting increase in our knowledge.

Preface

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Among the tens of thousands of documentary papyri from Roman Egypt, there survive just over three hun- dred census returns filed by ordinary Egyptian declarants.
text_raw:
Among the tens of thousands of 
documentary papyri from Roman Egypt, there survive just over three hun-
dred census returns filed by ordinary Egyptian declarants.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Extant returns run from AD 11/12 down to the last known census in 257/258, but the vast majority date to the second and early third centuries.
text_raw:
Extant returns 
run from AD 11/12 down to the last known census in 257/258, but the vast 
majority date to the second and early third centuries.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Their state of pre- servation varies: some are scraps, but many contain complete or nearly complete registers of Egyptian households.
text_raw:
Their state of pre-
servation varies: some are scraps, but many contain complete or nearly 
complete registers of Egyptian households.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: In all, nearly eleven hundred registered persons can now be made out, of whom sex is known for more than a thousand, and age for more than seven hundred.
text_raw:
In all, nearly eleven hundred 
registered persons can now be made out, of whom sex is known for more 
than a thousand, and age for more than seven hundred.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: About three- quarters of surviving returns come from the Arsinoite and Oxyrhynchite nomes (administrative districts), which lay in Middle Egypt to the south- west of the Nile Delta; other nomes are represented only intermittently.
text_raw:
About three-
quarters of surviving returns come from the Arsinoite and Oxyrhynchite 
nomes (administrative districts), which lay in Middle Egypt to the south-
west of the Nile Delta; other nomes are represented only intermittently.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although the Egyptian census returns are not free of the flaws that beset all pre-modern censuses, their surprisingly high demographic quality has long been recognized.
text_raw:
Although the Egyptian census returns are not free of the flaws that beset 
all pre-modern censuses, their surprisingly high demographic quality has 
long been recognized.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Early discussion of them from this standpoint cul- minated in Marcel Hombert and Claude Préaux’s classic Recherches sur le recensement dans |’Egypte romaine, published in 1952.
text_raw:
Early discussion of them from this standpoint cul-
minated in Marcel Hombert and Claude Préaux’s classic Recherches sur le

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Since then, how- ever, research has been spasmodic.
text_raw:
Since then, how-
ever, research has been spasmodic.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The only major demographic contribu- tion is Keith Hopkins’s 1980 article on “Brother-Sister Marriage in Roman Egypt.” Hopkins devoted much of this article to exploratory demographic comments on the census returns, which he argued “are far from perfect, but . . . the best data we have” for ancient populations.
text_raw:
The only major demographic contribu-
tion is Keith Hopkins’s 1980 article on “Brother-Sister Marriage in Roman 
Egypt.” Hopkins devoted much of this article to exploratory demographic 
comments on the census returns, which he argued “are far from perfect, but 
. . . the best data we have” for ancient populations.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Hopkins was the first historian who applied to the returns the sophisticated modelling techniques that modern demographers use when analyzing imperfect data.
text_raw:
Hopkins was the first 
historian who applied to the returns the sophisticated modelling techniques 
that modern demographers use when analyzing imperfect data.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
Frontmatter
text: XVi Preface In 1988, the co-authors of this book decided to extend Hopkins’s approach in a more sustained and comprehensive manner.
text_raw:
XVi Preface 
In 1988, the co-authors of this book decided to extend Hopkins’s 
approach in a more sustained and comprehensive manner.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Our aim was to examine what we both consider a fairly typical example of the ancient demographic regime, especially as it was experienced by quite ordinary individuals situated far beneath the Roman Empire’s social and political elite: farmers, laborers, soldiers, scribes, weavers, doctors, goldsmiths, gardeners, stone-cutters, ropemakers, donkey-drivers, and their families and households, all persons commonly met with in the Egyptian census returns.
text_raw:
Our aim was to 
examine what we both consider a fairly typical example of the ancient 
demographic regime, especially as it was experienced by quite ordinary 
individuals situated far beneath the Roman Empire’s social and political 
elite: farmers, laborers, soldiers, scribes, weavers, doctors, goldsmiths, 
gardeners, stone-cutters, ropemakers, donkey-drivers, and their families 
and households, all persons commonly met with in the Egyptian census 
returns.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
Frontmatter
text: The first was to collect all known returns, to verify their texts, and to publish demographically relevant information in a uniform catalogue.
text_raw:
The first was to collect all known 
returns, to verify their texts, and to publish demographically relevant 
information in a uniform catalogue.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The second was to employ modern methods in reconstructing the long-term demographic characteristics that the census returns can most probably be held to support for Roman Egypt.
text_raw:
The second was to employ modern 
methods in reconstructing the long-term demographic characteristics that 
the census returns can most probably be held to support for Roman Egypt.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Roger Bagnall took primary responsibility for the first part of the project, and Bruce Frier for the second; but at every stage we commented at length on each other’s drafts, and the resulting book is entirely collaborative.
text_raw:
Roger Bagnall took primary responsibility for the first part of the project, 
and Bruce Frier for the second; but at every stage we commented at length 
on each other’s drafts, and the resulting book is entirely collaborative.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Demography, as a social science, examines an extremely important aspect of human experience through an intellectual framework largely specific to it as a discipline.
text_raw:
Demography, as a social science, examines an extremely important aspect 
of human experience through an intellectual framework largely specific to 
it as a discipline.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although the techniques employed in this book may seem exotic to many ancient historians, all are in everyday use among modern historical demographers.
text_raw:
Although the techniques employed in this book may seem 
exotic to many ancient historians, all are in everyday use among modern 
historical demographers.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We intend our study to be as “user-friendly” as possible; therefore we carefully set out and explain the methods we use, but avoid congesting the text with equations and formulas that might confuse or intimidate.
text_raw:
We intend our study to be as “user-friendly” as 
possible; therefore we carefully set out and explain the methods we use, but 
avoid congesting the text with equations and formulas that might confuse or 
intimidate.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: However, we also provide bibliographic references to elemen- tary and more advanced demographic manuals describing these techniques, in the hope that interested readers will not only check our results, but also extend these methods to other sources.
text_raw:
However, we also provide bibliographic references to elemen-
tary and more advanced demographic manuals describing these techniques, 
in the hope that interested readers will not only check our results, but also 
extend these methods to other sources.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Throughout we try to be as clear as possible in defining technical terms, and more generally in explaining the conceptual framework of demographic research.
text_raw:
Throughout we try to be as clear as 
possible in defining technical terms, and more generally in explaining the 
conceptual framework of demographic research.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Readers who remain baf- fled may wish to consult a standard introduction such as Colin Newell’s Methods and Models in Demography (1988), a wonderfully lucid exposi- tion we draw on heavily.
text_raw:

fled may wish to consult a standard introduction such as Colin Newell’s 
Methods and Models in Demography (1988), a wonderfully lucid exposi-

text: Modern demography makes frequent use of models in order to evaluate imperfect statistical evidence about past populations.

Modern demography makes frequent use of models in order to evaluate

text: In our experience, these models can be a source of confusion in their own right.

In our experience,

text: Models such , as the ones we use are not infallible guides to demographic truth, and they have sharply limited historical worth independent of empirical data to which they are applied.

text: Preface XVii pated against the unanticipated, in a delicate effort to reconstruct, within the limits of available evidence, a unique historical population that is at once realistic and plausible.

text: As will emerge, this approach calls for discernment.
text_raw: As will emerge, this approach calls for discernment.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although demogra- phy may seem at times a rigorously statistical and hence ineluctable disci- pline, scholarly taste and judgment inform it at every stage, and such sub- jective factors assume greater consequence when, as is true of Roman Egypt, surviving data are incomplete and poorly preserved.
text_raw:
Although demogra-
phy may seem at times a rigorously statistical and hence ineluctable disci-
pline, scholarly taste and judgment inform it at every stage, and such sub-
jective factors assume greater consequence when, as is true of Roman 
Egypt, surviving data are incomplete and poorly preserved.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: In this respect, the demography of Roman Egypt does not differ from any other historical study of the ancient world; scanty surviving evidence is pressed to its limits, and at times doubtless a bit beyond.
text_raw:
In this respect, 
the demography of Roman Egypt does not differ from any other historical 
study of the ancient world; scanty surviving evidence is pressed to its 
limits, and at times doubtless a bit beyond.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We consider it essential that the seeming precision of our statistics not of itself induce false confidence in the result.
text_raw:
We consider it essential that the 
seeming precision of our statistics not of itself induce false confidence in 
the result.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: On the other hand, the census returns present historians with extraordinary opportunities, which it would be unfortunate to lose simply because the subject matter is unpalatable or numbers arouse suspicion.
text_raw:
On the other hand, the census returns present historians with 
extraordinary opportunities, which it would be unfortunate to lose simply 
because the subject matter is unpalatable or numbers arouse suspicion.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Even an approximate reconstruction of the major demographic functions for Roman Egypt has value, since so little is otherwise known about these functions in the ancient world; but the fine balance between mortality and fertility was certainly as fundamental to Greek and Roman civilization as to all other societies before the modern demographic transition.
text_raw:
Even an approximate reconstruction of the major demographic functions 
for Roman Egypt has value, since so little is otherwise known about these 
functions in the ancient world; but the fine balance between mortality and 
fertility was certainly as fundamental to Greek and Roman civilization as to 
all other societies before the modern demographic transition.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: As to demographic method, this book raises different issues: how well do modern techniques work when applied to an historical population known only through evidence that is of reasonably high quality, but sparse and scattered?
text_raw:
As to demographic method, this book raises different issues: how well do 
modern techniques work when applied to an historical population known 
only through evidence that is of reasonably high quality, but sparse and 
scattered?

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Do these techniques continue to yield generally credible results?
text_raw: Do these techniques continue to yield generally credible results?

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although the Egyptian census returns are, in this respect, virtually a limit- ing case, the techniques appear to hold up well.
text_raw:
Although the Egyptian census returns are, in this respect, virtually a limit-
ing case, the techniques appear to hold up well.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Modelling alone cannot eliminate all defects in the evidence; indeed, it often brings defects into sharper focus, thereby establishing the limits of our knowledge.

text: The documents and the history of the census This book is a study of the population of Egypt in the first three centuries of Roman rule.

The documents and the history of the census 
This book is a study of the population of Egypt in the first three centuries 
of Roman rule.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Its central questions concern the size and structure of Egyp- tian households, the population’s age and sex distribution, and the patterns of mortality, marriage, fertility, and migration that are likely to have prevailed in Roman Egypt.
text_raw:
Its central questions concern the size and structure of Egyp-
tian households, the population’s age and sex distribution, and the patterns 
of mortality, marriage, fertility, and migration that are likely to have 
prevailed in Roman Egypt.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The basis for all of this inquiry is a body of about 300 census declarations, of which the earliest dates to AD 12 and the latest to AD 259 (but survives only in a later copy, perhaps from around 266).
text_raw:
The basis for all of this inquiry is a body of 
about 300 census declarations, of which the earliest dates to AD 12 and the 
latest to AD 259 (but survives only in a later copy, perhaps from around 
266).

text: These declarations are by no means the only evidence for the ages of the residents of Egypt in this period, but they are the only sizable corpus of evidence that at least purports to provide complete rosters of particular households, whatever the age, sex, or status of their members.

chapter_title: Chapter 7, Sections 1 and 2 below.
text: However, as we tried to suggest above, actual households undoubtedly exhibited a much more intricate and irregular life cycle, alternating: erratically over generations between simpler and more complex forms.*® This inference is confirmed by seven households for which returns survive from two or even three successive censuses.4/ In 89-Ar-1 from Arsinoe, three brothers aged 30, 20 and 7 live together; the oldest brother is married to a woman aged 25.48 In the next census (103-Ar-8), the brothers are still together, but the oldest brother’s marriage has ended in divorce or his wife’s death; the youngest brother, now 21, is married to a woman aged 25, but there are still no children.

Stable populations 
The preceding description of a life table rests on an essentially static view 
of a population: a cohort of 100,000 persons is born at the same instant and 
then gradually dies, at given mortality rates, until no one is left.

the normal tendency in modern populations where females have a higher 
life expectancy than males.

chapter_title: Chapter 7 below (at notes 59-64). See also Chapter 8 and Table 8.1.
text: As it might seem, the most plausible cause of the sex ratio’s movement is that Egyptian males had a higher life expec- tancy than females, and therefore predominated in older ages.
text_raw:
As it might seem, the most plausible cause of 
the sex ratio’s movement is that Egyptian males had a higher life expec-
tancy than females, and therefore predominated in older ages.

chapter_title: Chapter 7 below (at notes 59-64). See also Chapter 8 and Table 8.1.
text: However, as will emerge below, this explanation is not without major difficulties; above all, because of the normal distribution of male and female mortality across their lifetimes, the sex ratios in the returns do not correspond to predictable patterns even in populations with higher male than female life expectancy.
text_raw:
However, as 
will emerge below, this explanation is not without major difficulties; above 
all, because of the normal distribution of male and female mortality across 
their lifetimes, the sex ratios in the returns do not correspond to predictable 
patterns even in populations with higher male than female life expectancy.

themselves.
